title: Minimum Incompatibility
statement: Split all the elements of `nums` into exactly `k` groups that each hold the same number of elements, `nums.length / k`. Every element goes into exactly one group, and no group may contain the same value twice. The incompatibility of a group is its largest value minus its smallest value. Return the smallest possible sum of the incompatibilities of the `k` groups, or `-1` if no valid split exists. The order of elements inside a group, and the order of the groups, do not matter.
notes:
## Intuition

With at most 16 elements, any set of positions fits in a 16-bit mask. Trying every assignment of elements to groups explodes, mostly because the same split is found once for every order of its groups. Two ideas fix that. First, precompute the cost of every valid group: a mask of exactly `size = n / k` positions with no repeated value. Second, build a split group by group in a fixed order: the next group must contain the lowest position not used yet, so each split is built only once.

## Approach

1. Sort `nums`. Then, reading a group in index order, its smallest value is at its `first` index, its largest at its last, and equal values sit next to each other.
2. For every `group` mask with `size` set bits (counted in `bits`), set `cost[group]` to largest minus smallest, unless two neighbouring members are equal; invalid masks keep `-1`.
3. `dp[mask]` is the least total cost of splitting exactly the positions in `mask` into groups. Start with `dp[0] = 0`.
4. For each reachable `mask`, take `low`, the bit of the lowest free position, and `rest`, the other free positions. Enumerate every subset `sub` of `rest`; if `sub | low` is a valid group, relax `dp[mask | group]`.
5. Return `dp[full]`, or `-1` if it was never reached.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [1, 2, 1, 4]` sorts to `[1, 1, 2, 4]`, `size = 2`. Valid groups (as position sets): `{0,2}` and `{1,2}` cost 1, `{0,3}` and `{1,3}` cost 3, `{2,3}` costs 2; `{0,1}` holds two 1s and stays `-1`.
- `mask = 0`: `low` is position 0, so try `{0,2}` (`dp[0101] = 1`) and `{0,3}` (`dp[1001] = 3`).
- `mask = 0101`: only `{1,3}` is free, giving `dp[1111] = 1 + 3 = 4`.
- `mask = 1001`: only `{1,2}` is free, giving `3 + 1 = 4` again.

So `dp[full] = 4`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(2^n · n) to price every group, plus one pass over the subsets of the free positions for each reachable mask: O(3^n) at worst, about 1.4 million steps for n = 16.
- Space: O(2^n) for `bits`, `cost` and `dp`.

## Pitfalls

- A value that appears more than `k` times makes any split impossible; `dp[full]` then stays `Infinity` and must be turned into `-1`.
- Without forcing `low` into the next group, each split is reached in every group order, and the search is far slower.
- The empty subset `sub = 0` must be tried too: it is the whole group when `size = 1`. That is why the loop tests `sub === 0` at the end.
- Repeated values are only forbidden inside one group: `[1, 1]` with `k = 2` is a valid split with cost 0.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `size` | elements per group, `n / k` |
| `full` | mask with all `n` positions |
| `bits` | number of set bits of each mask |
| `cost` | incompatibility of each valid group, `-1` otherwise |
| `first`, `previous` | lowest member of a group and the last one seen while scanning it |
| `dp` | least cost to split each set of positions |
| `free`, `low`, `rest` | unused positions, the lowest of them as a bit, and the others |
| `sub`, `group` | a subset of `rest`, and the candidate group: `sub` plus the `low` bit |
